newsitem.title: UK: BoE powerless to prevent b/society conversions.
newsitem.headline: BoE powerless to prevent b/society conversions.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George said on Wednesday that the conversion of building societies into banks, which is putting billions of pounds into consumers' pockets, could be a shock to the economy but the central bank had no powers to do anything about it.
Asked by the House of Commons Treasury Select Committee if the Bank should not have acted, he replied:
"I certainly don't think the Bank of England could have told converting building societies when and how to make their conversions and I'm rather sceptical whether the government could either."

"We do not have, under the Banking Act, any power to tell somebody that they may not apply for a banking licence this month because it happens to be inconvenient to us and/or the government for some other purpose," George added. "That is a matter for politicians."

The Bank of England had not been in a position to foresee that "windfall" gains from building society flotations would escalate in the way they did. The Bank has raised its estimates to around 35 billion stg from 20 billion earlier this year.
The windfalls would have an impact on inflation and the external accounts and the Bank was doing all it could to establish what their effects would be.
Asked what ideas the Bank had for offsetting the impact of the windfall gains, George replied: "I'm not sure myself that anybody has come up with any sensible ideas."
